about: Strategy cards for /debat. Each debater gets the same task and one card: a reasoning mode, a method and a priority. The dealer never repeats a card and spreads every entry as evenly as it can. Add or edit entries freely; ids must stay unique inside a list.

reasoning.name: First principles
reasoning.how: Reduce the task to facts and requirements that cannot be disputed, then rebuild the answer from those alone. Keep a convention only if it still earns its place.

reasoning.name: Pre-mortem
reasoning.how: Assume your answer has already failed in real use. Write down why it failed, then design the answer so that none of those failures can happen.

reasoning.name: Cross-domain transfer
reasoning.how: Find a solved problem from another field with the same structure. Transfer its solution, then repair every place where the comparison does not hold.

reasoning.name: Hostile reviewer
reasoning.how: Imagine the toughest expert who wants to reject your answer. List their objections first and build an answer that leaves them nothing to say.

reasoning.name: Constraints first
reasoning.how: List every hard limit, stated or implied: time, money, tools, format, audience, skills. Only then search the space that remains.

reasoning.name: Concrete case
reasoning.how: Work one real, fully specified example end to end before generalising. Let the example expose what the abstract answer would have missed.

reasoning.name: Socratic
reasoning.how: Question each assumption hidden in the task until only justified ones remain, and answer from those.

reasoning.name: Contrarian
reasoning.how: Start from the opposite of the obvious answer and argue for it seriously. Keep the obvious answer only if it survives that test.

reasoning.name: Systems view
reasoning.how: Map the parts, the flows between them and the feedback loops. Look for second-order effects and where a change upstream breaks something downstream.

reasoning.name: Quantitative
reasoning.how: Put numbers on everything that matters: sizes, costs, latencies, probabilities, effort. Decide with estimates, not adjectives.

reasoning.name: User journey
reasoning.how: Walk through the answer step by step as the person who will use it. Every point where they would hesitate or get stuck is a defect.

reasoning.name: Decomposition
reasoning.how: Split the task into independent sub-problems, solve each one well, then check that the pieces fit together without gaps.

reasoning.name: Evidence first
reasoning.how: Gather what can be checked before deciding: read the files, the docs, the data. Every important claim in the answer must point to its evidence.

reasoning.name: Option space
reasoning.how: Lay out at least three genuinely different approaches, compare them on the task's criteria, and commit to the best with reasons.

methods.name: Draft, critique, rewrite
methods.how: Write a full draft quickly, criticise it line by line as a reviewer would, then rewrite it from that critique.

methods.name: Outline first
methods.how: Fix the structure and the key points before writing any detail, then fill each part in.

methods.name: Test first
methods.how: Write the checks the answer must pass (tests, acceptance criteria, examples) before the answer, then build until all pass.

methods.name: Three drafts
methods.how: Produce three short, deliberately different drafts, keep the strongest, and graft in the best parts of the other two.

methods.name: Research then synthesis
methods.how: Collect the relevant facts and sources first, then write an answer that uses them, nothing more.

methods.name: Work backward
methods.how: Start from the finished result the user wants and derive each preceding step until you reach the current situation.

methods.name: Minimal, then harden
methods.how: Build the smallest answer that satisfies the task, then harden it against every failure case you can find.

methods.name: Requirement checklist
methods.how: Extract every requirement into a numbered checklist, answer each one explicitly, and verify none is left unticked.

methods.name: Iterate on examples
methods.how: Run the answer mentally (or for real) on several varied examples, including awkward ones, and fix it after each run.

methods.name: Explain to a learner
methods.how: Write as if teaching someone smart who knows nothing of the context. Gaps in the explanation reveal gaps in the answer.

priorities.name: Simplest thing that works
priorities.how: When in doubt, choose the solution with fewer moving parts that still meets every requirement.

priorities.name: Maximum rigour
priorities.how: Correctness above all: no unchecked claim, no hand-waving, every edge case handled or explicitly ruled out.

priorities.name: Robustness
priorities.how: Optimise for what still works when inputs are wrong, load is high or parts fail.

priorities.name: User value
priorities.how: Optimise for what the end user actually gains: clarity, time saved, fewer decisions for them to make.

priorities.name: Security and safety
priorities.how: Treat every input as hostile and every secret as precious. Close abuse paths before adding features.

priorities.name: Performance
priorities.how: Optimise for speed, memory and cost, with numbers to back each choice.

priorities.name: Maintainability
priorities.how: Optimise for the next person who has to read, change or extend this. Clear names, small parts, no cleverness without payoff.

priorities.name: Speed to ship
priorities.how: Optimise for something usable today; defer what can safely wait, and say what was deferred.

priorities.name: Completeness
priorities.how: Leave nothing for the user to fill in: every step, value, file and command present.

priorities.name: Evidence backed
priorities.how: Prefer the option you can prove with a test, a measurement or a source over the one that merely sounds right.

priorities.name: Standards and best practice
priorities.how: Follow the established conventions of the domain unless there is a stated reason not to, and name the convention you follow.

priorities.name: Originality
priorities.how: Look for the non-obvious answer that the others will miss, as long as it fully meets the task.
